claims.text: The original linear system has variables \(A_{\lambda,\theta}\) with \(\lambda\subseteq b^a\), \(|\lambda|<N\), and \(\theta\subseteq(n-r)^r\), \(|\theta|=N-|\lambda|\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 285-303]
The published large-\(N\) step enlarges \(\varphi\), then asserts that setting selected enlarged variables to zero recovers the original equations. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 777-818]

The proposed projected-wide-row repair that discards \(\theta\nsubseteq(q-i)^j\) is false: it discards an original variable \(A_{\varnothing,(2)}\). Take \[ (n,r,i,j,a,b,N)=(6,3,2,2,1,2,2),\qquad q=n-r=3. \] This is valid since \[ a+j=3=r,\quad a+i=3=q,\quad b=2\le i,j,\quad N=2=ab. \] The original variables are exactly \[ x=A_{\varnothing,(2)},\qquad y=A_{\varnothing,(1,1)},\qquad z=A_{(1),(1)}. \] Since \((q-i)^j=(1,1)\), the original variable \(x\) is excluded by the proposed projection. The original decomposable partitions of weight \(ij+N=6\) are \[ (3,3),\quad(3,2,1)\quad\text{(wide)},\qquad(2,2,2)\quad\text{(tall)}. \] Pieri gives their rows, in column order \((x,y,z)\), \[ \operatorname{Lin}(3,3)=(0,1,0),\quad \operatorname{Lin}(3,2,1)=(1,1,1),\quad \operatorname{Lin}(2,2,2)=(1,0,1). \] Hence the original wide-row lattice is \[ W=\mathbb Z(0,1,0)+\mathbb Z(1,1,1). \] For the first enlargement \[ (\widehat n,\widehat r,\widehat j)=(24,6,4), \] the partition \[ \tau=(4,2,2,2) \] is enlarged-wide and decomposable. Retaining **all** original variables in its row gives \[ P_{\rm all}\bigl(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\tau)\bigr) =(1,0,0), \] because \[ c_{(2^4),(2)}^{(4,2,2,2)}=1,\qquad c_{(2^4),(1,1)}^{(4,2,2,2)}=0,\qquad c_{(2^4,1),(1)}^{(4,2,2,2)}=0. \] But \((1,0,0)\notin W\): if \[ (1,0,0)=u(0,1,0)+v(1,1,1), \] then the first coordinate gives \(v=1\), whereas the third gives \(v=0\), a contradiction.

Therefore the asserted alternative “every enlarged wide row projects to an original wide row or zero” fails once every original variable is retained. In particular, the required extension-of-solutions argument is not supplied by the cited enlargement procedure.
No alternative all-valid-parameter proof of the original large-\(N\) inconsistency is provided here.
